questions.q: How does loose connective tissue differ from dense connective tissue?
options: More ground substance and cell types with fewer, thinner fibres
More tightly packed thick collagen bundles
Fewer cells and no ground substance
Fibres arranged only in parallel rows
questions.explain: Loose tissue looks airy because of abundant ground substance; dense tissue is packed with collagen.

questions.q: Which sites contain dense irregular connective tissue?

questions.q: What does each ring-shaped unit represent?
options: An osteon: concentric lamellae around a Haversian canal
A trabecula with marrow on each side
A cluster of chondrocytes in a lacuna group
questions.explain: Each osteon has concentric lamellae around a central canal carrying vessels and nerves.
questions.alt: Orange-brown to pale yellow ground section packed with concentric ring systems and bright blue-white holes.

questions.q: Why is this not cancellous bone?
options: It is built from osteons, not trabeculae with marrow spaces
It is made of elastic fibres
questions.explain: Cancellous bone has plates and struts with marrow between them; osteons mark compact bone.

questions.q: A biopsy from the umbilical cord shows abundant hydrated ground substance containing widely separated fibroblast-like cells and delicate collagen fibres. Which connective tissue is present?
questions.explain: Wharton's jelly is mucous connective tissue, characterised by abundant hydrated ground substance rich in hyaluronic acid and sparse cells and fibres. It cushions the umbilical vessels.

questions.q: In a connective-tissue section, a large cell contains numerous basophilic granules that release histamine and heparin during an immediate hypersensitivity reaction. Which cell is being described?
questions.explain: Mast cells are granule-rich resident connective-tissue cells. Their IgE-mediated degranulation releases histamine and other mediators involved in immediate hypersensitivity and inflammation.

questions.q: A lymph node reticular framework is examined with a silver stain. Which collagen type forms the delicate branching fibres that support lymphocytes and other free cells?
questions.explain: Reticular fibres are composed mainly of type III collagen. They form a delicate supporting meshwork in lymphoid organs, bone marrow and other soft organs.

questions.q: Which feature best distinguishes a unilocular white adipocyte from a multilocular brown adipocyte on routine histology?
options: White adipocytes contain many small lipid droplets and a central nucleus
White adipocytes contain one large lipid droplet that displaces the nucleus peripherally
Brown adipocytes contain no lipid inclusions
questions.explain: White adipocytes typically contain one large lipid droplet that pushes the nucleus to the cell periphery. Brown adipocytes contain multiple lipid droplets and abundant mitochondria.

questions.q: A multinucleated cell lies in a shallow depression on a bone surface and has a ruffled border facing the bone matrix. What is its principal function?
options: Storage of calcium within lipid droplets
questions.explain: Osteoclasts are multinucleated bone-resorbing cells derived from the monocyte-macrophage lineage. Their ruffled border increases the surface area for acid and enzyme-mediated resorption.
